dedupe_keys.name: cpmi iosco guidance on cyber resilience for financial market infrastructures 2016

description: The Guidance on cyber resilience for financial market infrastructures is an international supervisory guidance that applies the Principles for Financial Market Infrastructures (PFMI) to cyber risk for payment systems, central securities depositories, securities settlement systems, central counterparties and trade repositories. It covers governance, identification of critical functions and assets, protection, detection, response and recovery, testing, situational awareness and learning, and asks infrastructures to be able to pre-empt attacks, respond rapidly and achieve faster and safer recovery if an attack succeeds, working with participants and other stakeholders. It was published on 29 June 2016 by the Committee on Payments and Market Infrastructures at the Bank for International Settlements and the International Organization of Securities Commissions as CPMI Papers No 146. The 32-page PDF is free on the BIS site. Caveats: it is guidance, not binding rules, and national supervisors implement it differently; the page read summarises it without quoting specific targets. For simulation it defines the resilience objectives and recovery expectations that scenario analyses of cyber attacks on payment and settlement infrastructure should test. It is related to the ECB TARGET2 liquidity stress test record in this catalogue, which examines the resilience of one such infrastructure.
